briefing:
# Pre-Meeting Briefing: Canva, 17 November 2026

**Window:** Roughly 18 October to 17 November 2026. Sources found date from 2 to 10 November 2026.

## Summary
Canva has restructured sharply in early November, cutting about 22% of its staff. It has also expanded its AI partnership with OpenAI. Reports say a further round of cuts or a hiring freeze may follow, but Canva has not confirmed this.

## Restructuring and layoffs
- Canva is cutting 22% of its workforce, about 1,271 employees, as it flattens its org chart and consolidates teams (https://www.computerworld.com/article/3816579/tech-layoffs-this-year-a-timeline.html; https://m.economictimes.com/news/international/world-news/canva-layoffs-2026-meet-ceo-melanie-perkins-who-plans-to-give-away-80-of-her-billion-dollar-fortune-as-1271-jobs-are-cut/articleshow/135575689.cms).
- The company is merging its product, growth and platform teams and reducing "subspecialisation," which may leave remaining staff with broader roles (https://tech.yahoo.com/general/breaking-news/article/tech-layoffs-tracker-2026-all-the-job-losses-across-canva-squarespace-amazon-microsoft-apple-meta-and-others-141507340.html).
- CEO Melanie Perkins said "small changes won't be enough" and that Canva needs to "re-found" itself around small, empowered teams (https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-11-04/canva-restructure-job-losses/107344304).
- Departing staff receive at least six months' salary, plus a $US10,000 grant for those starting a business or community project (https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-11-04/canva-restructure-job-losses/107344304). They also keep company MacBooks and get a free year of LinkedIn Premium (https://m.economictimes.com/news/international/world-news/canva-layoffs-2026-meet-ceo-melanie-perkins-who-plans-to-give-away-80-of-her-billion-dollar-fortune-as-1271-jobs-are-cut/articleshow/135575689.cms).
- Capital Brief reported previously unreported finance-division cuts in January, with 32 roles made redundant (https://www.startupdaily.net/topic/business/canva-doubles-downw-with-openai-just-days-after-launching-its-2nd-in-house-ai-model).
- Reports say Canva could make further redundancies or impose a hiring freeze in November, against a revised revenue growth outlook. Canva has not confirmed this (https://www.peoplematters.in/news/strategic-hr/canva-layoffs-in-november-company-reportedly-weighs-job-cuts-or-hiring-freeze-53137).

## AI and partnerships
- Canva expanded its OpenAI deal, gaining broader access to OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra and GPT-5.6 models. The companies will work on making these models cheaper to run. No savings or costs were disclosed (https://www.startupdaily.net/topic/business/canva-doubles-downw-with-openai-just-days-after-launching-its-2nd-in-house-ai-model).
- The deal came days after Canva launched its second in-house AI model (https://www.startupdaily.net/topic/business/canva-doubles-downw-with-openai-just-days-after-launching-its-2nd-in-house-ai-model).
- OpenAI already powers Canva Code, which builds interactive designs, websites and apps from text descriptions (https://www.startupdaily.net/topic/business/canva-doubles-downw-with-openai-just-days-after-launching-its-2nd-in-house-ai-model).

## Marketing
- Canva launched a North America brand platform, "What Will You Canva Today?", created by agency GS&P (Goodby's first work). The campaign opened with TV spots, the first airing during NBC Sunday Night Football on 1 November (https://www.mediapost.com/publications/article/419113/canva-unveils-campaign-by-new-agency-gsp.html).

## Deals and hires
- **Hires:** No relevant Canva hires were found in the sources.
- **Acquisitions:** The only dated acquisitions in the sources are older than 30 days: Ortto (1 Apr 2026), Doohly ($30.00M USD, 1 Mar 2026), Scene Group and MangoAI (both 1 Feb 2026) (https://tavily.com/knowledge/company/wafeqPWRLzYp). No new deals in the window were found.

## Source caveats
Sources disagree on headcount ("1,271" in most reports; "just over 1,200" in Yahoo's tracker). The Tavily profile is undated and may be stale. No primary Canva statement was among the sources.

## Open questions
1. Is a further round of redundancies or a hiring freeze planned for November, and if so, in which teams?
2. How will the OpenAI deal and in-house models change Canva's cost structure and product roadmap, and what savings are expected?
3. What does the revised revenue growth outlook look like, and how do the restructuring and AI investments support it?
